  Number:  1055

  Updated: 2026-08-14T18:12:46Z

Description:
What was broken
Once the search service folds checkpoints into sessions (ENT-1595), legacy checkpoints — which have no session id — surface as session rows with an empty sessionId. The client dedup keyed on sessionId alone, so every one of those legacy sessions collapsed into a single row and all but one disappeared from results.
Why
The dedup assumed every session row carries a sessionId. That holds for modern sessions but not for legacy checkpoints folded server-side, whose only stable identity is their checkpoint id.
The fix
Dedupe by sessionId, falling back to checkpointId when sessionId is empty. Modern sessions are unaffected (they still key on sessionId); legacy folded sessions now each keep their own row.
Verified
Unit tests pass, including a new case covering folded legacy sessions with empty sessionId.

Reviewed trail #1055 (`fix(search): dedupe folded legacy sessions by checkpointId`, ENT-1595, branch `ent-1595-client-dedup-fallback`, 3 commits, +66/-3). It builds clean and the search tests pass. But I ran the deduper directly on both `main` and the branch, and the headline finding is that **the bug described in the commit message doesn't exist in the code being changed.**

## 1. The stated mechanism is wrong (blocking — needs a re-check of the real symptom)

The description says the client dedup "keyed on sessionId alone, so every one of those legacy sessions collapsed into a single row and all but one disappeared." That can't happen. `dedupSemanticResults` (`cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go:527`) short-circuits on an empty id:

```go
id := r.ResultID()
if id == "" {
    deduped = append(deduped, r)   // results without an id are ALWAYS kept
    continue
}
```

On `main`, `ResultID()` for a folded legacy session returns `""` (empty `SessionID` → `resultField` returns `""` → `rawString("id")` returns `""` because `rawFields` is only populated for untyped rows). I ran it against `main` with three legacy rows plus a genuine duplicate pair:

```
in=5 out=4 dupes=map[session:1]
kept: sessionID="" display="a"   ← all three legacy rows survive
kept: sessionID="" display="b"
kept: sessionID="" display="c"
kept: sessionID="s1" display="d"
```

So the direction of the actual defect is the opposite of the one described: legacy rows were never collapsed, they were **never deduped at all** — a repo mirrored across cells would double-report each legacy session. If someone reported legacy sessions genuinely missing from results, the cause is upstream (most likely the server-side fold) and this change won't fix it. Worth confirming the original symptom was reproduced and is verified gone end to end.

## 2. What the change does do — both good, just described wrong

Running the same probe on the branch:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| two distinct legacy rows | 2 kept | 2 kept ✅ |
| same legacy row from two cells | 2 kept (dupe leaks) | 1 kept ✅ |

Plus `ResultID()` now returns a real id for legacy rows, so they stop showing a blank ID column in the TUI (`search_tui.go:1221`) and a blank `"id"` in the agent-facing compact JSON (`search_cmd.go:1050`). Both are real improvements — the commit message just needs to say so instead of the collapse story.

Minor: those rows now carry `type: "session"` with a *checkpoint* id. The documented drill-down is `entire checkpoint explain <id>`, so that happens to work, but `entire session info <id>` won't. One sentence in the field comment would save someone the confusion.

## 3. No test at the level where the bug was claimed

Both new tests (`search_test.go:416`, `search_test.go:431`) exercise `ResultID`/`DedupID` in isolation. A single test calling `dedupSemanticResults` with legacy rows would have caught the wrong premise immediately — and it's the behavior that actually matters. I'd add it; I have the exact cases from the probe if useful.

## 4. The repo-qualification (commit 86659ea2d) is fragile in a way the tests don't cover

`DedupID` keys on `Org + "\x00" + Repo + "\x00" + CheckpointID` (`search/search.go:388`). That makes cross-cell dedup depend on two more fields agreeing exactly across cells. Measured on the branch:

```
legacy row, org/repo missing on one cell   in=2 out=2  ← dupe leaks
legacy row, casing skew across cells       in=2 out=2  ← dupe leaks
one cell lacks checkpointId (older cell)   in=2 out=2  ← dupe leaks
```

The casing case isn't hypothetical in this codebase — `resolveRepoFilters` (`search_cmd.go:597-600`) lowercases `FullName` precisely because "casing differences between the git remote (e.g. entireio/CLI) and the repo index (entireio/cli)" occur. At minimum `strings.ToLower` both components. Severity is low (both cells read the same control plane, so they'll usually agree), but it's free to harden.

## 5. Checkpoint rows still use the unqualified id

If checkpoint ids are "unique only WITHIN a repo" — the justification in the `DedupID` comment — then `TypeCheckpoint` rows have the identical hole, since they key on raw `c.ID`. Confirmed on the branch:

```
checkpoint rows, same id in two repos   in=2 out=1 dupes=map[checkpoint:1]   ← one silently dropped
```

Legacy checkpoint ids are 6 random bytes (`checkpoint/id/id.go:166`), so the collision space is only 2⁴⁸ — the same premise that motivated commit 2. In practice the two colliding rows also have to land in the same result page, so real-world probability is negligible either way; the point is that the codebase should pick one policy rather than qualify sessions and not checkpoints. Either apply it to both or drop commit 2. (If the server's synthetic session key is itself repo-qualified, mirroring it is the right call — I can't see the BFF from here, so that's worth stating explicitly in the comment.)

## 6. Stale comments after commit 2

Both `SessionResult.CheckpointID` (`search/search.go:121-124`) and `TestResultID_SessionFallsBackToCheckpointID` (`search_test.go:412-415`) say "the cross-cell dedupe (ResultID) falls back to it". Commit 86659ea2d moved the dedupe to `DedupID`; `ResultID` is now display-only. Small, but these were written to explain exactly the thing that changed.

Description:
What was broken
When the search service folds legacy checkpoints into sessions (ENT-1595), those rows arrive with an empty sessionId. In the CLI that caused two problems:
The cross-cell deduper skips rows with an empty id, so it never deduped legacy sessions at all — a repo mirrored across cells reported each legacy session twice.
Those rows showed a blank id in results (the TUI id column and the agent-facing compact JSON).
(Note: unlike the web BFF — whose deduper keyed empty sessionIds on "" and genuinely collapsed legacy rows — the CLI deduper short-circuits on an empty id, so its bug was the opposite: a duplicate leak, not a collapse.)
Why
Legacy checkpoints predate the sessionId attribute, so their only stable identity is their checkpoint id — which the CLI wasn't using for dedup or display.
The fix
Give a legacy folded session a real display id by falling back to its checkpoint id (no more blank id column / JSON field).
Dedupe on a repo-qualified key: checkpoint ids are unique only within a repo, so the key qualifies by org/repo (lowercased, to survive casing skew across cells). Genuinely duplicated legacy rows now collapse across cells; two repos' rows that happen to share a checkpoint id stay distinct. The same qualification is applied to raw checkpoint rows, which had the identical hazard.
ResultID stays the raw, machine-lookup id for display; a separate DedupID carries the repo-qualified identity.
Verified
Unit tests plus a deduper-level test over legacy rows: distinct rows kept, mirrored rows collapsed, casing skew handled, cross-repo rows not collapsed.

Re-reviewed at `4dfbf19a9`. All four findings are resolved, and the follow-up commit is a genuinely good response — it fixed things properly rather than papering over them:

- Checkpoint rows now repo-qualified via a shared `repoQualifiedCheckpointKey` helper, not a copy-paste of the session branch
- `strings.ToLower` on both components, with the `resolveRepoFilters` precedent cited in the comment
- A real `dedupSemanticResults`-level test (`search_v4_test.go`) covering distinct/mirrored/casing-skew/cross-repo
- Stale comments corrected, plus the `entire session info` drill-down caveat I'd only mentioned in passing
- The description now describes what the code actually did, and the parenthetical reconciling the CLI's duplicate-leak against the BFF's genuine collapse is the right way to handle it — it explains where the original narrative came from instead of quietly deleting it

`go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and the full `cmd/entire/cli` + `search` suites are clean.

Three things in the new work.

## 1. Commit rows are the remaining hole in the "one policy" claim (medium)

The commit message says "One policy for both," and `DedupID` at `search/search.go:389` justifies the exemption:

> (Commit SHAs and session/repo ids are already global, so they pass through.)

Commit SHAs are globally unique as *content addresses*, but the same commit legitimately lives in many repos — that's what a fork is. Measured on this commit:

```
cm: same SHA, upstream + fork (two repos)   in=2 out=1 dupes=map[commit:1]   ← one silently dropped
cm: same repo mirrored across cells         in=2 out=1                       ← correct
```

So a search spanning `acme/backend` and a fork of it drops one repo's hit for every shared commit — the same user-visible failure (a valid result silently disappears) as the checkpoint collision this commit just closed, and considerably more likely, since forks share SHAs by design whereas the 12-hex checkpoint collision needs a 2⁴⁸ birthday hit landing in the same result page. Repo-qualifying commits is also safe for the intended case: mirrors of the *same* repo carry the same org/repo, so they still collapse.

Either extend the qualification to `TypeCommit`, or narrow the comment's claim and say why fork-shared SHAs are acceptable to collapse.

## 2. Checkpoint rows inherit the org/repo skew fragility (low)

```
cp: org/repo missing on one cell   in=2 out=2   ← duplicate leaks
```

Before this commit, checkpoint rows deduped on the bare id and were immune to this. The qualification now puts that dependency on the *most common* row type, in exchange for guarding a collision with negligible practical probability. Lowercasing handles the skew I raised last round; absence is the remaining one. Low severity — both cells read org/repo from the same control plane — but it's worth being deliberate that the trade got applied to the highest-volume type rather than inherited by symmetry.

## 3. The deduper-level test still only covers legacy sessions (low)

The lesson from round 1 was to test `dedupSemanticResults` rather than the id function in isolation. Checkpoint rows got brand-new deduper behavior in this very commit, but their only coverage is `TestDedupID_RepoQualifiesCheckpointScopedIDs` — the isolated form. The four cases in `TestDedupSemanticResults_LegacySessions` apply verbatim to checkpoint rows; adding them (or table-driving over both types) closes the same gap for the type that just changed.

- **Deduper test table-driven** over session/checkpoint/commit with all four cases per type, replacing the legacy-session-only version. This is the better fix — I'd suggested adding checkpoint cases; folding all three into one table is what actually keeps the next type from being forgotten.

`DedupID`'s comment now enumerates which ids repeat across repos and which pass through — and closes with:

> Repo ULIDs and real session ids are globally unique, so they pass through.

`TypePR` isn't in either list, despite being a live result type (it has its own `counts.PRs` bucket at `search_v4.go:659`). It falls through to `ResultID()` → `rawString("id")`, unqualified. Probed at this head:

pr: same id, two repos       in=2 out=1 dupes=map[pr:1]   ← collapses
pr: ResultID="42" DedupID="42" ResultRepo="backend" ResultOrg="acme"
repo: same ULID across cells in=2 out=1                   ← correct

The probe does confirm the mechanics are in place either way: PR rows expose `ResultOrg()`/`ResultRepo()`, so qualifying them is a one-line change if it turns out to be needed.

Given the comment is now the canonical statement of which ids repeat, I'd want PRs named in it explicitly — either "PR ids are ULIDs, global" or added to the switch. One line, and the next person doesn't have to re-derive it. That's the whole of it; nothing else outstanding, and I'd be comfortable with this landing once PRs are classified.

One semantic caveat if the tag is corrected: `matchedCheckpointId` is the checkpoint that *matched this query*, not a stable session identity. It's fine for cross-cell dedup of a single query (both cells run the same query against identical mirror content), but it means a legacy row's displayed id varies by search term. ## Verified working

A real session row pulled from the cell today, decoded through this head:

```
real row:  sessionID="019e3459-…" Matched="2bac5530d12a" ResultID="019e3459-…" DedupID="019e3459-…"
folded:    sessionID=""            Matched="2bac5530d12a" ResultID="2bac5530d12a"

round-trip: Matched="2bac5530d12a" (emits key=true)
```

That's the whole intended behavior, live: the field populates, a real session still keys on its `sessionId`, a folded row gets its checkpoint id for display and a repo-qualified key for dedup, and the field survives marshal/unmarshal so `--json` now carries it. Previously all three of those were `""`.

Rename is complete — no stale `CheckpointID` references outside the test function's name, which is fine as a description. The mixed-id-space comment correction landed accurately. Build, `gofmt`, `vet` clean; `cmd/entire/cli` and `search` suites pass. Final scope is 4 files, +197/−13.

## One thing left: the fold PR names the field `checkpointId`

The commit message says `checkpointId` "only exists in the unmerged fold PR." That's the part I can't see from here, and it's exactly the ordering hazard:

```
fold w/ checkpointId only: Matched="" ResultID="" DedupID=""
```

If the server-side fold merges emitting `checkpointId` for folded rows — the name it uses today, per your own commit message — the CLI goes inert again for precisely the rows this feature exists to handle, and the failure is silent (blank ids, no dedup, no error). The CLI is now correct for every row that exists *now*, and correct after the fold *only if* the fold switches to `matchedCheckpointId` before or with its merge.

Accepting both names removes the cross-repo merge-ordering dependency for about three lines — a `checkpointId` alias read in `UnmarshalJSON`, or a second field consulted as a fallback. Worth it given the two repos merge independently and nothing fails loudly if the assumption breaks. If the fold PR is already being updated to `matchedCheckpointId`, then this is a non-issue and only worth a sentence in the comment recording that the two names were reconciled deliberately.

Everything else is resolved. Your High finding is still marked `open` — it's fixed by this commit, so it wants resolving. Note also the approval is still recorded against `4dfbf19`, now four commits behind head.
